entities.name: PMID:10731497
observations: In 12 men with severe hypertriacylglycerolemia, 6 weeks of fish-oil n-3 ethyl esters (~3.4 g/day; EPA 49.1%, DHA 32.2%) reduced postprandial chylomicrons by 49–64% at 4–8 hours and VLDL by 36–43% at 4–8 hours.
Large chylomicron remnants decreased 19% at 6 hours and 43% at 8 hours; small remnants decreased 31% only at 8 hours.
Fasting VLDL-triacylglycerol decreased 44%; the study concluded that chylomicron and VLDL lowering was earlier and more consistent than remnant lowering.

entities.name: n-3 fatty acids
observations: Fish-oil n-3 ethyl esters were administered for 6 weeks at approximately 3.4 g/day in the relevant severe hypertriacylglycerolemia study.

entities.name: Postprandial lipoprotein lowering
observations: In severe hypertriacylglycerolemia, n-3 fatty acids lowered postprandial chylomicrons and VLDL more effectively and earlier than chylomicron remnants: chylomicrons 49–64%, VLDL 36–43%, versus remnant reductions mainly at 6–8 hours.
